title: Tunisian full stitch tote bag
excerpt: A structured tote bag in aran yarn worked in Tunisian full stitch. The dense, stable fabric holds its shape well and suits everyday use.
sourceNotes: Tunisian full stitch inserts through both the vertical bar and the horizontal strand, creating a thicker fabric popular for bags and home goods.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Tunisian stitch where the hook is inserted through both the vertical bar and the horizontal strand behind it. The result is a denser, thicker fabric than simple stitch.
A seam that joins two pieces by slip stitching through the edge stitches of both panels at once. It produces a neat, low-profile join on the outside of a bag.
A narrow strip of Tunisian stitches worked to a long length to form a bag handle. Starting width is 6 to 8 stitches for a comfortable flat strap.
A separate rectangle of Tunisian crochet that forms the bottom of the bag. It is joined to the body with a flat seam before the sides are worked.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 sts x 12 rows = 10 x 10 cm in Tunisian full stitch.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 35 cm wide x 40 cm tall (excluding straps).

14 sts x 12 rows = 10 x 10 cm in Tunisian full stitch.
Chain 50. Work Tunisian full stitch for 14 rows (approx. 10 cm). Fasten off.

Chain 50. Work Tunisian full stitch for 48 rows (approx. 40 cm). Fasten off. Join one long edge of each body panel to each long edge of the base panel using a flat seam. Then seam the short side edges of the body panels together.
Chain 9. Work Tunisian full stitch for 80 rows (approx. 60 cm). Fasten off. Attach each strap 8 cm from the side seams on the front and back panels, sewing through the top two rows of the bag body.
Weave in all ends. Work 1 round of dc around the top edge of the bag to neaten it.
